title: The Circuit Builder
summary: Combine capacitors in series, parallel and mixed networks, then find the energy stored and lost.
subject: physics
concepts: Energy lost when charge is shared
learningOutcome: The student can find the equivalent capacitance of series, parallel and mixed networks, the charge and voltage on each capacitor, the stored energy, and the energy lost on sharing charge.

levels.title: In a chain
levels.adds: Baseline: in series the same charge sits on each capacitor, 1/C = Σ 1/Cᵢ, and the voltages add up (Ex 2.6).
hints: The same charge Q = CV sits on every capacitor in the chain.
The voltage across one capacitor is Q divided by its own capacitance.

levels.title: Side by side
levels.adds: New idea: in parallel each capacitor has the full voltage and the capacitances add (Ex 2.7).
hints: In parallel the capacitances simply add.
Every capacitor has the full battery voltage across it.
Charge on one capacitor is Q = CV with its own C. pF × V gives pC, so divide by 1000 for nC.

levels.title: A mixed network
levels.adds: More steps: combine one group first, then treat it as one capacitor in the rest of the circuit (Example 2.9).
hints: Find the group that is purely in series or purely in parallel, and replace it by its equivalent.
Then combine the result with the remaining capacitor.
The battery sees one equivalent capacitor, so Q = C_eq V.

levels.title: Energy in the field
levels.adds: New idea: the energy stored is U = ½CV², so doubling the voltage multiplies it by four (Ex 2.10).
hints: U = ½CV², which is also ½QV and Q²/2C.
With C in pF and V in volts, ½CV² is in pJ; divide by 1000 for nJ.
The energy depends on the square of the voltage.

levels.title: The lost energy
levels.adds: New idea: sharing charge conserves charge but not energy; the difference is dissipated (Ex 2.11, Example 2.10).
hints: The total charge before is C₁V, and it is the same after, spread over C₁ + C₂.
The common voltage is the total charge divided by the total capacitance.
Work out ½CV² before and after and subtract.

misconceptions: The voltage is the same across capacitors in series
The charge is the same on capacitors in parallel
Energy is conserved when charge is shared between capacitors
